## Report on `region.fasta` (locus_007)

**Sequence:** 3,000 bp, single record. Composition G 864, C 787, A 682, T 667 — **GC 55.0%**, and GC is fairly uniform across the region (52.8–58.2% per 500 bp window). No unusual base composition.

### Main finding: an in-frame 33-bp tandem repeat

The one striking feature is a **tandem repeat array of a 33-bp unit, spanning 1864–2160** (~10% of the sequence).

- **Copies 1–8: 1864–2127** — 264 bp of essentially perfect tandem repetition, with per-copy identity to the consensus of 94–100% (each copy differs at only 0–2 positions). Coordinates: 1864–1896, 1897–1929, 1930–1962, 1963–1995, 1996–2028, 2029–2061, 2062–2094, 2095–2127.
- **Copy 9: 2128–2160** — a degenerate/divergent copy (only 54.5% identity to the consensus), after which the tandem repetition stops.
- Consensus unit: `GTCCTGAGGGCCATTGAGCGTACATCATCTCAT` (52% GC).
- A partial, degenerate match to the unit's 3′ half also occurs at **1831–1863** (i.e. at the start codon of the ORF described below), so the array may extend slightly further in vestigial form.

Variable positions among the eight conserved copies (relative to the consensus) are concentrated at unit positions 6, 26, 27, 28 and 31.

### Because 33 bp = exactly 11 codons, the repeat is protein-coding

The array is **stop-free in one reading frame**, so it encodes an **11-amino-acid tandem repeat**. (The unit contains TGA in two of the three forward frames and in two of the three reverse frames, so only specific frames are translatable — this is why the repeat is frame-locked.)

- **Forward ORF, 1831–2237** (ATG at 1831, stop TGA at 2236–2238), **135 aa**. Protein:
 `MRRGAMRTSCHV|LRAIERTSSH|VLRAIERTSSH|VLRAIERTSSH|VLRAIDRTSSH|LLRAIERTSSH|ILRAIERTSCH|VLRAIERRSSH|VLRAIVRTSSH|VLRAIERTSSH|VMRAIEVSNK|SSSIFPTIPSGINVVQCRTVSSGTVR`
 → a non-repetitive N-terminus (12 aa), **8–9 tandem copies of an 11-residue repeat (consensus `VLRAIERTSSH`, variants `VLRAIDRTSSH`, `LLRAIERTSSH`, `ILRAIERTSCH`, `VLRAIERRSSH`, `VLRAIVRTSSH`)**, then a non-repetitive Ser-rich C-terminal tail (last repeat is degenerate, `VMRAIEVSNK`). This is the classic architecture of a repeat-domain protein.
- **Reverse-strand ORF, 1610–2122**, **171 aa** (the longest ORF in the region). It covers the same array and reads the repeat in the other frame as an 11-residue repeat with consensus `EMMYAQWPSG`/`MMYAQWPSGH`, flanked by non-repetitive sequence. Both strands therefore present plausible repeat-containing ORFs; without a homology database search neither can be assigned to a known function.

### Minor observations
- Homopolymer runs: `GGGGGG` at 25–30, `AAAAA` at 122–126, `CCCCCC` at 2494–2499, `AAAAAA` at 2742–2747, and an `AAAAAAAA` run at 2955–2962 (within an A/T-rich/low-complexity stretch around 2945–2965).
- Several other short ORFs exist (e.g. 731–1063, 111 aa; 172–458, 96 aa on the reverse strand), but none is remarkable.
- No other tandem or interspersed repeat longer than ~20 bp was detected anywhere else in the 3 kb; the 33-bp array is the only strong repeat signal.

### Bottom line
This is a GC-rich (55%) 3,000-bp region whose notable feature is a **33-bp tandem repeat array at 1864–2160 (eight conserved copies 1864–2127 plus one degenerate copy 2128–2160)**. Because the unit length is a multiple of three and the array is stop-free in one frame per strand, it encodes a **tandemly repeated 11-residue peptide** — `VLRAIERTSSH` in the forward ORF 1831–2237 (135 aa) and `EMMYAQWPSG` in the reverse ORF 1610–2122 (171 aa). Everything else in the sequence looks like ordinary, non-repetitive DNA; nothing else stands out. Note that this analysis is database-independent — no similarity/homology searches were possible, so the biological identity of the repeats (e.g. a satellite DNA or a repeat domain in a protein) cannot be confirmed here.
